title: From cotton field to T-shirt: primary, secondary and tertiary jobs
examples: What are the three sectors of the economy?
Is a teacher a tertiary job?

stages.label: Cotton farm
stages.note: Primary: grow or dig raw materials.

explain.say: Look at the T-shirt you are wearing. How many people helped make it? Probably hundreds, in several countries! Look at the board: a T-shirt's journey, from cotton field to shop, step by step.

draw.text: From cotton field to T-shirt: primary, secondary and tertiary jobs

stages.label: Cotton farm
stages.note: Primary: grow or dig raw materials.

explain.say: See the cotton farm? Growing crops, fishing, mining and forestry are the primary sector, which means jobs that take raw materials from nature. Cotton might grow in India, the USA or Burkina Faso. Can you name another primary job?

stages.label: Cotton farm
stages.note: Primary: grow or dig raw materials.

explain.say: Next, the mill and factory: the secondary sector, jobs that make things from raw materials. Cotton is spun, woven, then sewn, perhaps in Bangladesh, the world's second biggest clothes exporter. What else is made in factories?

stages.label: Cotton farm
stages.note: Primary: grow or dig raw materials.

explain.say: Now the ship, the truck and the shop: the tertiary sector, which means services. Drivers, shopkeepers, teachers, doctors and coders do not make things; they do things for people. Which sector is your teacher in?

explain.say: Let's sort some jobs! Look at the three boxes. As countries get richer, more people move from farms to factories and then to services. Great sorting! Wow: in the UK more than eight in ten workers now have service jobs.

groups.label: Tertiary
groups.ask: Why do people move from farms to services?

faq.a: The primary sector takes raw materials from nature: farming, fishing, forestry and mining.
The secondary sector turns raw materials into products: factories, building, baking and making electricity.
The tertiary sector provides services rather than goods: shops, transport, health, education, banking, tourism and IT.

faq.q: Why do people move from farms to services?
faq.a: As countries develop, machines make farming need fewer workers, factories grow, and later people spend more on services like health, travel and entertainment.
asks: Why do sectors change as countries grow?

faq.a: Some economists add a fourth sector for knowledge work, such as research, software and information services.

facts: Bangladesh is the world's second-largest exporter of clothing, after China.
In India, about 45 percent of workers are in agriculture, while in the UK more than 80 percent work in services.

quiz.say: A fisher works in which sector?
quiz.show: A fisher works in which sector?
quiz.why: Fishing takes a raw material straight from nature.

wrong.1: Secondary jobs make products, like a fish-canning factory.
wrong.2: Tertiary jobs give services, like selling fish in a shop.

quiz.show: Which of these is a tertiary job?

wrong.0: Mining takes raw materials from the ground, so it is primary.
